newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cabinet approves deficit draft 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cabinet approves deficit draft 1997 budget.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday approved its 1997 draft state budget with a planned overall deficit of 36.9 billion crowns, the finance ministry said.

"The government approved the draft for the 1997 state budget with expected revenues at 170 billion crowns and expenditures at 206.9 billion crowns, so the overall deficit should total 36.9 billion," finance ministry spokesman Jozef Mach told Reuters.

The budget draft will be presented to parliament for final approval by November 15, Mach said. He added the deficit was increased after discussion with all budget-funded subjects, but he declined to elaborate further.
The final budget proposal is based on assumpted growth in gross domestic product (GDP) of at least six percent in 1997 with inflation for the year at under six percent, Mach said.
The GDP should total some 660 billion crowns in 1997.
The 1996 state budget deficit is planned to total 27 billion crowns.
Slovakia's state budget deficit totalled 13.4 billion crowns for the January-September period, up from a 7.9 billion crown shortfall for the first eight months of 1996.
Some 25 billion crowns of the planned deficit for 1997 are to be used for the country's debt servicing.

This means that according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) standards the 1997 fiscal deficit should total only some 11.658 billion crowns, representing 1.8 percent of the forecast GDP, Mach said.
In 1996 the fiscal deficit calculated according to IMF standards is planned to total some 14.4 billion crowns, or 2.5 percent of the GDP.
